summary: Two one-thread runs on the frozen T1 manifest reproduced every deterministic routing, tensor-payload, loss, gradient, optimizer, model, cache, and recovery-result field. The four warm expert processes used 17,913,408 safetensors bytes, 55.75% below the matched full process. Cold expert fan-out used 51,477,024 bytes, 5.34% above full. Stable and replacement expert result bytes matched after an accepted assignment was terminated. Expert final current RSS was lower, but pre-entry high-water RSS was higher, so no peak-memory saving is established.

measurements.label: Expert final current RSS reduction, minimum
Expert final current RSS reduction, maximum

guardrails.detail: Across both runs and both assignments, centralized-to-full-process and centralized-to-expert-process raw-gradient, clipped-gradient, and complete-model maximum differences were 0.0. Gradient, optimizer, and model SHA-256 values matched.

The full worker received the 8,390,904-byte frozen head once and each of four stable expert workers received it once. Every stable child completed two forward calls and stopped with semantic head SHA-256 855e5fce384d980d728e4534c8605ea0c4a24b1a44dcec111d69e37d7f7cc984.

Expert zero authenticated assignment zero, exited -15 after deliberate termination, and was replaced. The replacement exited 0 and returned the same 2,236,032-byte safetensors result with SHA-256 413d4c517068592b544ff25000aab0b80d5aaa56536b2b7b1750731012fef320; the replacement result was used in canonical reconstruction.

Cold and warm safetensors totals repeated exactly. JSON control bytes were recorded separately; environmental timing text changed one cold expert control and one warm full control by one byte between runs. Recovery payload remained outside the matched totals.
The evidence declares sequential worker scheduling and a maximum of one simultaneous worker child. RSS is reported per child, never as concurrent or aggregate colony memory.

findings.label: Process-separated expert reconstruction is exact
findings.description: The coordinator reconstructed both isolated one-step updates with byte-identical trainable state outcomes despite routing expert work through four persistent children.

findings.label: The warm traffic advantage survives process transport
findings.description: After both paths retained the same immutable head, the four expert processes used 55.75% fewer safetensors bytes and 55.73% fewer total application payload bytes than the matched full process.

findings.label: One accepted expert assignment recomputed exactly
findings.description: A replacement process loaded the same authenticated state and returned the stable result byte-for-byte. Post-loss recovery took 3.37 to 3.84 seconds and the separate loss control moved 23,508,639 application payload bytes.

findings.label: Cold expert fan-out remains more expensive
findings.description: Sending the 8,390,904-byte head to four new expert children left the cold expert safetensors total 5.34% above full and total application payload 5.36% above full.

findings.label: The process high-water mark does not show a memory saving
findings.description: Expert final current RSS was 34.05% to 34.54% below the matched full child, but expert high-water RSS was already dominated by interpreter and import startup and ended 3.75% to 4.36% higher. The experiment therefore establishes no peak-memory reduction.

findings.label: Worker timing is not an end-to-end speed result
findings.description: Expert round trips omit coordinator shared-trunk, routing, reduction, clipping, and optimizer work. Sequential scheduling also does not measure concurrent expert throughput.

limitations: This is a systems control, not a practical model campaign. It uses frozen T1 tokens and dimensions with a randomly initialized experimental sparse tracer; it does not train or evaluate a useful model.
The two assignments are independent one-step controls from identical initialization. They do not refresh routing and trainable state through a sequential optimizer trajectory.
The sparse tracer has one shared decoder block and four token-wise MLP experts. It is not the six-layer volunteer decoder trained in the historical T1 campaign.
The trusted-local spawned-pipe scope is not untrusted remote authentication, sandboxing, hostile-payload safety, or proof that public donated computation occurred.
SHA-256 identities detect local frame mismatch and bind evidence fields, but a malicious process that controls its own acknowledgements remains outside scope.
Worker processes ran one at a time. No concurrent throughput, aggregate RSS, network latency, packet framing, congestion, compression, or remote retry was measured.

Current RSS is sampled only at lifecycle boundaries. Linux high-water RSS includes pre-entry interpreter and import startup, differs between process runs, and cannot isolate model-compute peak in this harness.
The recovery control keeps the coordinator alive, pauses the first child cooperatively after assignment acceptance, and does not persist a boundary transaction or survive coordinator loss.
The frozen head is retained only for the life of each stable process. Replacement reloads it; no cross-process disk cache is established.
Capacity routing forced 128 tokens to every expert by rerouting 34 and 41 of 512 tokens. Equal counts are policy intervention, not evidence of learned specialization.
Application payload means serialized safetensors and canonical JSON payload bytes. Private multiprocessing frame headers and operating-system transport overhead are excluded.
No campaign training work or volunteer hardware donation was accepted in this local control, so it creates no contributor-credit entries.
